objectives: Show everything from 11.1 Floating and sinking and 11.2 Using ideas about density, exam style.

practice.prompt: Complete the sentences. Not every word is used.

items.sentence: An object floats on a liquid if it is ___ than the liquid.
An object floats when the upthrust is ___ its weight.
A denser liquid has more massive particles, so it gives a ___ upthrust.

practice.explanation: Less dense floats; floating means upthrust = weight; denser liquid → bigger upthrust.

practice.prompt: A block of wood has a mass of 450 g and a volume of 600 cm³. Calculate its density. Show your working and give the unit.

markPoints.point: Correct formula or substitution (mass ÷ volume, or 450 ÷ 600)
Answer: 0.75
Unit: g/cm³

practice.modelAnswer: density = mass ÷ volume = 450 g ÷ 600 cm³ = 0.75 g/cm³
practice.explanation: 1 mark working, 1 mark answer, 1 mark unit. 1.33 means the sum was upside down.

practice.prompt: Will the block of wood in question 2 float or sink in water? Explain your answer.

markPoints.point: It floats
Its density (0.75 g/cm³) is less than water's (1.0 g/cm³)
accept: less than the density of water
lower than the density of water
smaller than the density of water

practice.modelAnswer: It floats, because its density (0.75 g/cm³) is less than the density of water (1.0 g/cm³).
practice.explanation: Compare with water: 0.75 is less than 1.0 → floats.

practice.prompt: Use these densities: petrol 0.7 g/cm³, water 1.0 g/cm³, mercury 13.6 g/cm³. Tick (✓) whether each object floats or sinks.

rows.explanation: 0.75 is more than 0.7, so the wood sinks in petrol.
7.8 is less than 13.6, so steel floats on mercury.

practice.explanation: Compare the object with the liquid it is in, not always with water. Two correct rows = 1 mark.

practice.prompt: A submarine is under the water. Explain how it uses its ballast tanks to return to the surface. Use ideas about density.

markPoints.point: Air is pumped into the tanks and pushes the water out
The mass of the submarine decreases (volume stays the same)
Its density becomes less than the density of (sea)water, so it rises

practice.modelAnswer: Air is pumped into the ballast tanks, pushing the water out. This decreases the submarine's mass, while its volume stays the same, so its density becomes less than the density of seawater and it rises to the surface.
practice.explanation: Air in, water out → mass down → less dense than seawater → rises.

practice.prompt: Most solids are denser than their liquid form. Explain why ice is different and floats on water.

markPoints.point: Water expands / takes up more space when it freezes
So ice is less dense than water

practice.modelAnswer: When water freezes it expands and takes up more space, so ice is less dense than liquid water and floats.

practice.prompt: Use the particle model to explain why a boat floats higher in salt water than in fresh water.

markPoints.point: Salt water is denser / its particles are more massive
Its particles collide with the boat with a bigger force, giving a bigger upthrust

practice.modelAnswer: Salt water is denser, so its particles are more massive. When they collide with the boat from below they exert a bigger force, so the upthrust is bigger and the boat floats higher.
practice.explanation: Denser liquid → more massive particles → bigger push from collisions → bigger upthrust.

practice.prompt: Al-Biruni used a flask with a side arm to measure the volume of a gemstone. Describe his method.

markPoints.point: Fill the flask until water overflows through the side arm
Empty the beaker and put it back
Lower the stone into the flask
Measure the volume of water that overflows into the beaker
accept: measure the volume of the water
measured the volume of the water

practice.modelAnswer: Fill the flask with water until it overflows through the side arm. Empty the beaker and put it back under the side arm. Lower the stone into the flask. Measure the volume of the water that overflows into the beaker: this equals the volume of the stone.
practice.explanation: Any three of the four steps, one mark each.

practice.prompt: Explain why people in Al-Biruni's time needed a reliable way to identify gemstones.

markPoints.point: Cheaper stones (quartz, glass) look like real gems / diamond
So people could cheat / make a lot of money by pretending a fake was real

practice.modelAnswer: Cheaper stones such as quartz and glass look like real gems such as diamonds, so people could make a lot of money by pretending that a fake stone was real.
practice.explanation: Looks alike → people cheat for money.

practice.prompt: Tick (✓) whether each statement is about PRECISION or ACCURACY.

rows.statement: How close a measurement is to the true value.
rows.explanation: Close to the true value = accurate.

rows.statement: How close repeat measurements are to each other.
A thermometer that shows the correct temperature.
rows.explanation: Correct = close to the true value = accurate.

practice.explanation: Precision: small steps, readings agree. Accuracy: close to the true value.

practice.prompt: Describe one way scientists worked in the past that is SIMILAR to how they work today, and one way that is DIFFERENT.

markPoints.point: Similar: they build on the work of earlier scientists
Similar: they do experiments / take careful measurements / use density
Different: then often alone, now usually in teams
Different: then many topics, now they specialise
Different: now they publish and share results worldwide / use new technology

practice.modelAnswer: Similar: scientists then and now build on the work of earlier scientists. Different: in the past scientists often worked alone, whereas today they usually work in teams.
practice.explanation: One similarity + one difference. Two of the same kind only scores 1.

summary: density = mass ÷ volume, in g/cm³. Always show working and the unit.
Compare the object's density with the LIQUID it is in: less dense floats, denser sinks.
Floating: upthrust = weight. Denser liquid → more massive particles → bigger upthrust.
Ice floats because water expands when it freezes. Submarines change their mass with ballast tanks.
Al-Biruni: overflow method for volume, very precise densities. Precise ≠ accurate. Then alone, now teams.

flashcards.front: Wood (0.75 g/cm³) is put in petrol (0.7 g/cm³). Float or sink?
Steel (7.8 g/cm³) is put in mercury (13.6 g/cm³). Float or sink?
How does a submarine return to the surface?
flashcards.back: Air pushes water out of the ballast tanks, its mass decreases, and it becomes less dense than seawater.

flashcards.front: What are the 4 steps of the overflow method?
flashcards.back: Fill the flask until it overflows; empty the beaker; lower the stone in; measure the water that overflows.

flashcards.front: Precise or accurate: close to the true value?
What is the same about scientists then and now?
flashcards.back: They build on the work of earlier scientists.
